$schema-note: Consumed by tools/ci/arb_translate.py `extract`. `doNotTranslate` lists proper nouns/brands/acronyms that must be copied verbatim into every locale. `terms` maps dance-domain jargon to a short note pinning the *intended* meaning, so an assisted translation (or a human) renders the dance sense rather than an everyday homograph (e.g. `caller` is the person who prompts the dance, not a telephone caller). This is guidance, not a hard gate; keep it small and high-signal.

caller.note: The person who teaches and prompts a social dance in real time. NOT a telephone caller. Many languages keep the English 'caller' as a loanword in the folk-dance community — prefer the established local term only if one genuinely exists.

call.note: The spoken prompt a caller gives dancers (verb: to call a dance). Dance-instruction sense, not a phone call.

set.note: The formation of dancers on the floor (e.g. a longways set), or the act of 'setting' as a step. NOT a collection, a settings screen, or 'to set a value'.

figure.note: A named dance movement/pattern (e.g. swing, allemande, hey). NOT a number, illustration, or 'to figure out'.

formation.note: How dancers are arranged before dancing (duple improper, Becket, Sicilian circle, longways, etc.). A structural dance term.

progression.note: How couples move to a new position each time through the dance so they meet new neighbors. A contra/longways structural term, not general 'progress'.

proper.note: A formation state where dancers are on their standard side (opposite of 'improper'). Dance-technical term, not 'correct/appropriate'.

improper.note: A common contra formation where certain dancers have crossed to the opposite side. Dance-technical term — NOT 'inappropriate'.

indecent.note: A specific duple formation name (a variant of proper/improper). Dance jargon — do NOT render as 'obscene'.

hey.note: A weaving figure where dancers pass in a set pattern (a 'hey for four'). A dance figure, not the interjection 'hey'.

allemande.note: A turn where dancers grasp arms/hands and rotate. Keep as 'allemande' unless a well-established local dance term exists.

balance.note: A dance figure: step and balance toward/away from a partner. The step sense, not financial/equilibrium 'balance'.

swing.note: A buoyant rotating figure danced with a partner. The dance figure, not a playground swing or musical swing.

promenade.note: A figure where a couple travels together in a hold. Dance sense.

neighbor.note: The dancer(s) you dance with besides your partner, changing as the dance progresses. Dance-role term.

partner.note: Your primary dance partner for the whole dance. Dance-role term.

square.note: A dance form / formation for four couples in a square. When it labels the dance form, it is a proper form name.

contra.note: A folk dance form danced in long lines of couples. Keep as 'contra'.

mixer.note: A dance in which you change partners over the course of the dance. Dance sense, not a kitchen mixer or audio mixer.

program.note: In this app: a caller's curated, ordered list of dances for an event/evening. NOT a computer program/application. This is a core app noun.

collection.note: In this app: the user's personal library of saved dances. App noun.

dialect.note: In this app: the configurable mapping from canonical move names to the words a particular caller/community uses. App feature name — see the dialect system.

shorthand.note: In this app: a caller's abbreviated notation for a figure. App noun.

duple.note: A minor set of two couples (duple minor). Dance structural term.

triple.note: A minor set of three couples (triple minor). Dance structural term.

longways.note: A formation of couples in two long facing lines. Dance formation name.
